speaker: yolandaaguilar
text: Thank you, Madam Mayor and members of the City Commission. I'll try to be as brief as possible. Over the last couple of weeks, I want to say months, and it seems like dog years, we've been involved with the CARES reimbursement process, as well as FEMA, for any and all eligible expenses as a result of the pandemic. As you know, we provided to you an Excel spreadsheet at the beginning of the process that basically outlined some of the projects that you, as well as our office, recommended for reimbursement. That list got a thumbs-up from Miami-Dade County, from Jennifer Moon. I think you all saw my emails. She thought it was a great list. After attending numerous webinars and informational sessions via Zoom and in conversation with a consultant for Miami-Dade County, it's a company by the name of Hagerty, and they've been very responsive. We find that some of the projects that you and the City felt it was important to assist the residents, that unfortunately, these programs would either entail additional resources. And I want to go through these three categories, because I think it's important that we put on record that, while the intention is noble and on the part of the Mayor and Commission, unfortunately, it doesn't rise to the level of the reimbursement process. So the first thing that they have basically stated is, as you know, we talked about a gift card for groceries for senior citizens who live on fixed income using the threshold that Miami-Dade County has established for the additional homestead exemption. Basically, the City would have to invest $25,000 based on $100 per household, per family, on an estimate of 250 families. The City would have to invest $25,000 in cash expense to purchase the gift cards and basically create a project that would be subject to approval from FEMA and CARES. And there are no guarantees that this project will be reimbursed because we have to prove that certain conditions exist in every single household. So we would be having to have a member of staff or additional staff to actually ask for financial statements and pretty much the financial status of each and every family considered for these grocery cards. So I'm very weary, especially what we have been talking about and just talked about, about the upcoming financial outlook. And I think every City needs to be very concerned about this in the next couple of years in suggesting to you that you make an expense of this magnitude and later come to you and say that it is not going to be reimbursed by CARES or FEMA. So, I mean, we've done our due diligence, but there are no guarantees that we will be reimbursed. And again, FEMA will reimburse the City for expenses related under Category B titled Protective Emergency Measures. And I don't know that this would fall under that category. And we've dealt with FEMA for many years. And again, CARES would have such scrutinization of the project that I am not confident that we should be earmarking or spending $25,000 in this project. Secondly, we spoke about the opportunity of allowing small businesses or businesses in general along our corridors a grant for $2,500 to make it equal for everybody to help them maybe go out there and market their services once the reopening phases start. And we're looking that some of these businesses are now going to be allowed to reopen. And so we thought about coming up with ways that the City could give a direct benefit, although we understand that the County has been given and the federal government has all these programs that are available to businesses. And I know, Mayor, that you had talked to me about the possibility of this grant program and other commissioners, the Vice Mayor, everybody had reached out to our office. However, I am advised that because the accountability for the program would be so complex and the program criteria become so stringent that it would require us to have to at least at a minimum hire staff that would work with each individual business and obtain financials, obtain ownership records, obtain bank statements, and have a pro forma pretty much of everything that they have lost along the way since March 16th. Actually, the designation date is April 1st. If we wanted to put the money on the table for this program, you're talking about $750,000, give or take, based on 300 businesses. So I'm not confident that we are able to hire new staff for this project. And I am not confident that we have a software that they will require for us to continue measuring the goals of the program and the performance by each and every business. So I would like to ask for your pretty much staff to be devoted to having a liaison with the business community and asking for things that are, you know, that are financially sensitive, if you would. Not all businesses would qualify. Off the top of my head, I can tell you, Publix will not qualify because they have made a lot of money during the pandemic. They have a lot of surpluses. They have a lot of grants for businesses like that. Grocery store chains that we have in our city. Gas stations. You know, people that have not really lost a lot of money will not be eligible to receive the $2,500. And of course, we would not be reimbursed. So on and on, I can tell you that developing these programs are extremely difficult for the city. Again, the water bill reduction, I know we talked about giving residents of the city, every household, a one-time $50 water bill reduction. We have been advised by CARES, by Meredith Moore and Andre, which are the representatives for Hagerty. We have already been advised that the reduction in the water bills is not a CARES eligible approved activity. So unfortunately, the three categories which you all and we felt that would be of tremendous assistance to the community and it would put us out there on a very positive note, there are no guarantees that we can recover this money. So what we're doing now, we're in the process of filing our reimbursements for actual, for the plexiglasses that have been installed at city hall, for the 1% that's coming to you for our first responders shortly at the next commission meeting, the employee time, the sanitation equipment and supplies that the city has had to purchase, the signage for the wearing of the masks, the time for the employees from the recreation center assigned to help out with the delivery of the second meals being funded by district six and it's a partnership. So we have about $65,000, $70,000 worth of real expenses that have already gone on into the books that we believe that we can be reimbursed for and we will be reimbursed for. It's not going to be an overnight decision. You saw it in Irma. You've seen it in past storms that there are hoops that you have to jump and it takes about 18 months to two years during any given major episode to collect money from FEMA because of the scrutiny and the paperwork and the trail involved with following up on this. So I wanted to give you this report which I will follow in writing. I did start to issue the memo but over the last few days I've been extremely involved with CARES and FEMA. There's a lot of entry work that has to be done and Mrs. Leong and I have undertaken this responsibility but I will confirm this in writing but I think it was important enough for residents to understand the magnitude of the paperwork and the compliance issues and the accountability issues that are involved with participating in these programs. It all sounds really nice. Well, apply for this and we'll give it to you. Well, that's not the way it works.
